audit.whatIsWrong: Three places (spikes[3].text, late, whys[6]) claim Zac's Let's Bounce! knock-up is 'exactly the airborne Yone wants' for a Q3-R chain. Fate Sealed has no airborne requirement at all.
audit.why: Riot's text for Fate Sealed: 'Yone blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him.' There is no airborne prerequisite anywhere in it — that condition belongs to Yasuo's Last Breath, and it appears to have been copied across to Yone. Separately, Yone's own Q3 knock-up lands on HIS enemies, so a knock-up Zac applies to Yone's team could not feed it either. The practical damage is the same as in the Yasuo entry: Zac players are told their ultimate is a liability when it is not.
audit.corrected: Fate Sealed needs no airborne setup, so your R never feeds it — the reason to time R is his 80-120s ult itself, not a chain.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (Last Breath — where the airborne requirement actually lives)

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound (E) is described as 'snaps back to safety' without the one detail that makes it exploitable.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Yone's spirit leaves his body behind... When this ability ends, Yone's spirit is forced back to his body." The body is a visible, stationary anchor and the return is forced, not optional. That means Zac knows exactly where Yone will be when E expires — which is a charged Elastic Slingshot waiting on a known destination. E is 22/19/16/13/10s, so at rank 1 the punish window after it is long.
audit.corrected: His body is a fixed marker for where he must return — charge E onto the body and he is forced into it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave (W) is treated as a flat shield every trade, with no note on what sizes it or when it is available.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Grants a shield to Yone, the value is increased by the number of champions hit by the swipe' and 'Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed.' In a 1v1 lane he is only ever hitting one champion, so it is the minimum-size shield, and at base attack speed the 14s cooldown is long. Both facts make his early trades far less oppressive than the current text implies.
audit.corrected: In lane his W shield only ever hits one champion, so it is the small version, and at base attack speed it is a 14s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers appear anywhere in this matchup.
audit.why: Mortal Steel is 4s, Spirit Cleave 14s before attack speed, Soul Unbound 22s at rank 1, Fate Sealed 120s at rank 1. The R number matters most: at 120 seconds, "wait until his R is down" is a two-minute window, not a brief one.
audit.corrected: Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1 — a dodged or baited ult buys you an entire wave cycle.

edits.before: Fate Sealed (R) at 6 lets him wait out your Elastic Slingshot engage and then dash-slam you back to his side; combined with his Q3 knock-up he can airborne-chain you the moment you commit.
edits.after: Fate Sealed (R) at 6 lets him wait out your Slingshot engage and then pull you back to his side. It needs no airborne setup, so nothing you do enables it — but at 120s, baiting it once buys a wave cycle.

edits.before: After his first crit or on-hit item Yone's sustained DPS through W-shield outpaces your tankiness, and his E soul-return heal undoes the damage you managed to land.
edits.after: After his first crit or on-hit item Yone's W-shield DPS outpaces your tankiness, but his E return is forced onto his own body — pre-charge E where that body stands.

edits.before: In fights your Let's Bounce! knock-up is exactly the airborne Yone wants to chain his Q3 and R, so a loose engage sets him up — you must engage only when his R is down and your team follows.
edits.after: In fights your Let's Bounce! does not feed him — Fate Sealed needs no airborne setup, so there is no chain to hand him. Engage on his R cooldown because it is 120s, not because your knock-up helps him.

edits.before: From 3-6 he stays ahead — his E, Soul Unbound, lets him commit aggressively and then snap back to safety, undoing your counter-damage, and at 6 Fate Sealed (R) can wait out your Slingshot engage and slam you back, so never dive him with his ult and Q3 both available.
edits.after: From 3-6 he stays ahead — Soul Unbound (E) lets him commit and repeat his damage on the way out — but the return is forced onto his body, so charge E where the body is standing. At 6 Fate Sealed pulls you back to him; it is 120s, so bait it.

edits.before: With 2+ items Yone's shielded, mobile DPS keeps this matchup his; worse, your R knock-up is the airborne he wants for his Q3-R chain, so a greedy Let's Bounce! feeds him — engage only when his R is on cooldown and your teammates are there to convert the CC before he E's back out.
edits.after: With 2+ items Yone's shielded, mobile DPS keeps this matchup his, but your R is not the liability the old read suggested — Fate Sealed requires no airborne, so Let's Bounce! never sets him up. Engage on his 120s R cooldown, with teammates there to convert the CC before he E's out.

edits.before: At 6 Fate Sealed (R) waits out your engage and slams you back, flipping any dive to him.
edits.after: At 6 Fate Sealed pulls you back to him, but at 120s a baited ult is a free wave.

edits.before: With 2+ items your R knock-up feeds his airborne chain, keeping the matchup his into teamfights.
edits.after: With 2+ items his shielded DPS still keeps it his, but your R never feeds his Fate Sealed.

edits.before: Wait out his Q3 dash and R before committing your E engage
edits.after: Charge E onto his body — Soul Unbound forces him back

edits.before: Use Q3 and R knock-ups to chain-airborne you when you dive
edits.after: Pull you back in with Fate Sealed the moment you commit

edits.before: E-knock his combo — sustain his Q3, out-trade. Zac wins the Soul Unbound cooldown windows.
edits.after: E-knock his combo, and charge E onto his body. Zac wins the Soul Unbound cooldown windows.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — He snaps back when it ends. E-knock in it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Yone Soul Unbound: 22s at rank 1, and the return to his body is forced — charge E onto the body. - Spirit Cleave: 14s at base attack speed, minimum shield in a 1v1. - Fate Sealed: 120s at rank 1, no airborne needed.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Soul Unbound's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The lane-control window: Soul Unbound is 22s and always ends on his body, so bank your leads there. If behind, farm safe.

edits.before: Elastic Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Yone's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1 and needs no airborne setup, so your own knock-ups never hand him the fight. Bait it out.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Soul Unbound: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Trade strictly around Soul Unbound: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, hold E for his forced return to the body.

edits.before: Elastic Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight — build your teamfight around that. Yone carry threat: 9/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight, and Fate Sealed needs no airborne, so your R never feeds it. Yone carry threat: 9/10 — anti-heal stays core if he gets ahead.

notes: Same class of error as the Yasuo entry: the airborne-chain premise was copied onto Yone, whose Fate Sealed has no airborne requirement whatsoever. It appeared in spikes[3].text, late and whys[6] and told Zac players not to ult. Cross-layer disagreement left in place: content win[] gives Yone 7/7 while full phases[].side gives Zac 4/7. Yone genuinely wins the matchup (48.54% for Zac over 342 games), so the content chart is the defensible one and I did not flip cells — but the full layer's phase sides contradict its own data and should be regenerated. Packet suspectNames are both FALSE POSITIVES: "Let's Bounce" (the '!' is present in the file, the detector strips it) and "Use Cell Division" ('Use' is the preceding verb, the ability name is correct). NOT VERIFIED and left alone: whether Zac's Q or E can hit Yone's body while he is in spirit form, and whether Fate Sealed's pull can be interrupted mid-cast.
